rv.q: Xia’s production is very entertaining indeed.
Matthew Xia is a director of swagger and finesse.
As this sharp satire swerves from sex comedy to sweet study of male intimacy, the acts they become a part of end up being less gratuitous and altogether more tender than they may have expected.
Harris and director Matthew Xia give us an incredibly tender portrayal of vulnerability and driftlessness.
Tender is an interesting and fresh look at toxic masculinity; what lies beneath the surface when men confront their inner feelings and realise that there’s always someone else to consider.
Tender is a wildly entertaining play that balances comedy with emotional depth, while sharing a unique exploration of masculinity.
Tender is another excellent drama in this space that reaches out to men who are conditioned to conform and stay quiet about their problems and any self-doubt.

cn.t: Harris's sharp satire of masculinity at a failing strip club wins praise for its swagger and sincerity, swerving from raunchy comedy to tender exploration of male intimacy with bold theatricality and affecting depth.
